title: When the Letters Falls
premise: Emrys Dravenmoor, a celebrated wedding planner whose own engagement ended in scandal, is coerced into judging a city-wide anonymous letter-writing program meant to rekindle connection among strangers. A clerical error pairs her with Julian Voss, the rival planner who testified against her years ago, and neither realizes it at first—until the letters become the only honest place either of them has left. When their identities surface mid-competition, Emrys must choose between exposing the corruption that ruined her and protecting the man who helped bury it, while a deadline on the program's final gala forces both to decide whether love is worth the truth that could destroy it. In the end, Emrys testifies to the full story, forfeits the career she built on hiding, and meets Julian after the last train leaves—choosing to let him stay.
about_author: Beatrix Delacroix is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's happily-ever-afters before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal cottage where she keeps every letter anyone has ever sent her.

chapters.title: The Last Train Metaphor
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At a lavish wedding she orchestrated, Emrys watches the bride's father quietly leave early and feels her cynicism harden into doctrine: love is a performance she no longer believes in. Her assistant announces the city's pen-pal initiative needs celebrity judges. Emotional beat: numb professionalism cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Assigned Correspondents
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian Voss, riding high on a merger that absorbed half his competitors, signs up for the letter program as PR damage control after a scathing profile calls him 'love's undertaker.' He receives his first anonymous letter—and answers more honestly than he intended. Emotional beat: guarded curiosity he refuses to name.

chapters.title: Ink Without Faces
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The letters deepen: Emrys confesses her broken engagement without names; Julian admits he testified against a colleague to save his company, without saying which. Neither recognizes the other's voice. Meanwhile they clash viciously in person over a shared venue contract. Emotional beat: intimacy growing in one place while hostility calcifies in another.

chapters.title: What the Merger Buried
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Digging through old contracts for the gala, Emrys finds evidence the merger that elevated Julian was built on forged signatures—including hers. Her anonymous correspondent's confession suddenly reads differently. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling toward someone she's never seen but already trusts.

chapters.title: The Gala Guest List
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian realizes his pen pal's phrasing matches Emrys's spoken cadence and panics, nearly withdrawing from the program. Instead he writes a letter begging forgiveness for something unnamed. Emotional beat: cowardice wrestling with a conscience he thought he'd amputated.

chapters.title: Programmed to Fail
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys discovers the letter program itself is a front—the mayor's office using it to launder goodwill for the very development deal that destroyed her business. Her letters to Julian become coded warnings. Emotional beat: rage finding a target, and tenderness complicating it.

chapters.title: Unmasked at Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the program's midpoint mixer, an organizer accidentally reveals pairings. Emrys and Julian stand face to face, each holding the other's last letter. The confrontation is quiet and devastating—he doesn't deny the testimony; she doesn't deny wanting to forgive him. Emotional beat: betrayal and longing arriving simultaneously.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian offers Emrys everything: documents, testimony, his resignation—if she'll let him do it publicly, for her, not just for his conscience. She refuses charity disguised as redemption and demands he tell the whole truth including his own guilt. Emotional beat: pride and love negotiating terms neither can fully honor.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Climax. At the gala, instead of her prepared speech endorsing the program, Emrys exposes the corruption—naming Julian as accomplice first, then reading aloud his unsent letter of confession. The room fractures; the deal collapses; her career likely ends. Julian takes the stage beside her uninvited. Emotional beat: truth chosen over safety, together.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV closing on Emrys. Months later, disgraced but lighter, Emrys plans one small wedding for free—a couple who met through the real letters. Julian appears at the empty station platform where her engagement once ended, past the last departure. She lets him stay. Emotional beat: belonging earned through ruin, love in present tense at last.
